gaps.sentence: If dogs ___ wings, they would fly.
gaps.hint: an impossible present, past simple if-clause
gaps.explanation: Impossible present conditions still take the past simple after 'if': had.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: What will you do if the train ___ before you get there?
gaps.explanation: Even in questions about the future, the if-clause uses the present simple: leaves.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ green.
gaps.explanation: The adverb 'always' signals a timeless result, so the present simple fits: get.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ faster — we might still catch the train.
gaps.hint: if only plus could, present inability
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'could' expresses a present inability you regret: could run.

gaps.sentence: If the appeals court ___ the verdict, the case will be reheard in the autumn.
gaps.explanation: Present simple after 'if', will + infinitive in the main clause.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.
